items.title: No-Self, Verses 10–16: Why Defilement Still Has Real Causes

items.zh: 由二品為依，是生便可得。恒於境放逸，又復邪昇進。愚癡之所漂，彼遂邪昇進；諸貪愛所引，於境常放逸。
items.en: Resting on these two kinds — the householder and the renunciant — the arising and the attainment [of defilement] come about: constantly heedless towards objects, and again advancing along a wrong path. Carried along by delusion, one advances along a wrong path; drawn along by craving, one is constantly heedless towards objects.

items.zh: 由有因諸法，眾苦亦復然。根本二惑故；十二支分二。自無能作用，亦不由他作，非餘能有作，而作用非無。
items.en: Because there are phenomena with causes [the first seven links], so too are there sufferings with causes [the last five]; because of these two root afflictions, the twelve links divide into two groups. Nothing produces its own action by itself, nor is it produced by another; nor does anything else have the power to produce it — and yet the function is not simply absent.

items.zh: 非內、亦非外，非二種中間。由行未生故。有時而可得。設諸行已生，由此故無得；未來，無有相。過去，可分別。分別曾所更，非曾，亦分別。行，雖無有始；然有始可得。
items.en: Not within, not without, not in between the two: because these formations have not yet arisen, [defilement] can at times be found. Should one posit these [future] formations as already arisen, by that very positing they are not found, since the future has no mark; only the past can be discerned. One discerns what one has already experienced, yet what has not been experienced can also be discerned; though conditioned things have no beginning, still a beginning can be found.

items.title: No-Self, Verses 17–26: Ten Verses on Purification — Same Emptiness, Now Applied to Freedom

items.zh: 諸色，如聚沫，諸受，類浮泡，諸想，同陽焰，諸行，喻芭蕉，諸識，猶幻事，曰親之所說。諸行一時生，亦一時住、滅。癡，不能癡癡，亦不能癡彼；非餘能有癡，而愚癡非無。不正思惟故；諸愚癡得生。此不正思惟，非不愚者起。
items.en: Form is like a heap of foam; feeling is like a floating bubble; perception is like a mirage; formations are like a plantain trunk; consciousness is like a conjured illusion — so the Kinsman of the Sun himself declared; conditioned things arise in a single moment, and in a single moment abide and cease. Delusion cannot deceive itself, nor can it deceive another; nor does any other possess delusion — and yet delusion is not simply absent. Because of improper attention, delusion comes to arise; and this improper attention arises only in one who is already deluded, never in one who is free of delusion.

items.zh: 福非福不動行、又三應知，復有三種業，一切不和合。現在，速滅壞，過去，住無方，未生，依眾緣，而復心隨轉。畢竟共相應，不相應亦爾。非一切一切，而說心隨轉。
items.en: Meritorious, demeritorious, and unmoving formations — formations should, again, be known as threefold [past, future, and present]; and there are, further, three kinds of action — none of them ultimately combine with anything at all. What is present quickly perishes; what is past abides nowhere; what has not yet arisen depends on many conditions — and yet the mind is spoken of as flowing on accordingly. Whether ultimately conjoined or ultimately not conjoined, it is never simply everything conjoined with everything — and yet the mind is spoken of as flowing on accordingly.

items.zh: 於此流無斷，相似不相似；由隨順我見，世俗用非無。若壞於色身；名身亦隨滅。而言今後世，自作自受果。前後差別故，自因果攝故；作者與受者，一異不可說。
items.en: Within this uninterrupted stream — sometimes similar, sometimes dissimilar — because it accords with the view of a self, its conventional function is not simply absent. If the physical body is destroyed, the name-body [the four mental aggregates] likewise ceases with it; and yet it is said that in this life and the next, one reaps what one has sown. Because of difference between what came before and what comes after, yet because both are gathered within one and the same causal stream, whether the doer and the one who experiences the result are the same or different simply cannot be said.

items.title: No-Self, Verses 27–31: How Self-View Itself Arises Without Any Self Behind It

items.zh: 因道不斷故，和合作用轉；從自因所生，及攝受所作。樂戲論為因，若淨不淨業。諸種子異熟，及愛非愛果。
items.en: Because the causal stream is never broken, its combined function continues to operate: arising from its own proper cause, and [itself] taking up what has been done. Delight in conceptual proliferation, and action pure or impure, are the causes: [the first] of the ripened body of all the seeds, [the second] of agreeable and disagreeable results.

items.zh: 依諸種異熟，我見而生起；自內所證知，無色，不可見。無了別凡夫，計斯為內我。我見為依故，起眾多妄見。總執自種故，宿習助伴故；聽聞隨順故，發生於我見。
items.en: Resting on the ripening of these seeds, the view of a self arises; it is known only through one's own inner experience — formless, and so not visible to others. The unperceiving ordinary being takes this to be an inner self; and resting on this self-view, many further false views arise. Because of the wholesale grasping of one's own seeds, because of habituation carried from before and its companion [unsound attention], and because of hearing and following along with what one hears, the view of a self comes to be generated.

items.title: No-Self, Verses 32–44: Suffering's Grip, and the Forty-Four Verses Close

items.zh: 貪愛及與緣，而生於內我。攝受希望故，染習外為所。世間真可怖，愚癡故攝受；先起愛藏已，由茲趣戲論。彼所愛藏者，賢聖達為苦。此苦逼愚夫，剎那無暫息。不平等纏心，積集彼眾苦。積集，是愚夫計我、苦、樂、緣。諸愚夫固著，如大象溺泥。由癡，故增上，遍行、遍所作。
items.en: Craving, together with its object [the storehouse consciousness], gives rise to the sense of an inner self; through taking hold of what is already had, and longing for what is not, one becomes habituated to treating the outer world as one's own. The world is truly fearsome, yet the deluded still cling to it; having first taken up this cherished clinging, one then proceeds into endless conceptual elaboration. What is thus cherished and clung to, the noble ones recognise as suffering itself; this suffering presses upon the deluded moment after moment, without the slightest respite. An unbalanced mind entangled in affliction accumulates these many sufferings; it is the deluded who accumulate it — this suffering being the condition for conceiving a self, and for pain and pleasure. The deluded cling fast, like a great elephant mired in mud; through delusion, it is dominant [over the other two sufferings], pervading [every feeling], and pervading all that is done.

items.zh: 此池派眾流，於世流為暴。非火風日竭，唯除正法行。於苦計我受，苦樂，了知苦；分別此，起見，從彼生，生彼。染污意，恒時諸惑俱生滅。若解脫諸惑；非先，亦非後。
items.en: This pool sends forth many streams, more violent than any worldly flood; neither fire, nor wind, nor sun can dry it up — only the practice of the true Dharma can. Towards suffering, one conceives a self that experiences pain and pleasure — know that both rest on suffering; the discriminations arising from this give rise to views — arising from that same source, and in turn giving rise to it again. The defiled mind [manas], at every moment, arises and ceases together with its afflictions; when freed from these afflictions, it is neither freed before them nor after them.

items.zh: 非彼法生已、後淨，異而生。彼先無染污，說解脫眾惑。其有染污者，畢竟性清淨。既非有所淨；何得有能淨。諸種子滅故，諸煩惱盡故；即於此無染，顯示二差別。
items.en: It is not that a defiled state first arises, and then, afterwards, a separate purity arises to replace it; that mind was, from the start, never actually defiled — this is what is meant by liberation from the afflictions. What appears defiled is, in its ultimate nature, already pure; since there is nothing there to be purified, how could there be anything that purifies it? Because the seeds are extinguished, and because the afflictions themselves are exhausted, this very freedom from defilement reveals two distinct kinds of liberation.

items.zh: 自內所證故，唯眾苦盡故。永絕戲論故，一切無戲論。眾生名相續，及法想相中，無生死流轉，亦無涅槃者。
items.en: Because it is realised only within, because it is simply the exhaustion of all suffering, because conceptual elaboration is utterly cut off — in this, there is no conceptual elaboration whatsoever. Within what is called "a sentient being's continuity" and within the notion of "phenomena," there is, in truth, neither one who flows on through birth and death, nor one who attains nirvāṇa.

blocks.text: Today you read the rest of the forty-four verses of ultimate meaning on non-self, in Ru-Yi's translation. They are dense, and the prose commentary that explains them follows over the next three days. Read the verses once today without worrying about every line; the commentary below gives their shape.

Defilement rests on two classes, householders and renunciants. Venerable Miào Jìng: "householders live in craving, so all their defilements come from craving"; renunciants are carried by delusion onto wrong paths. He adds, via Master Cháng Bǎi, a warning: "if a hundred people who haven't learned non-self practise meditation, all hundred will cling to meditation."

Two root afflictions divide the twelve links: ignorance most powerful in initiating karma, craving in moistening it (Day 65). Defilement arises not from future formations, which do not yet exist, but from present and past ones: "though formations have no beginning, a beginning can be found", in the present moment where defilement is newly produced.

Purification begins by contemplating the aggregates as like foam, bubbles, mirages, plantain trunks, and illusions (the five similes), and then their shared mark: arising and ceasing together. Master Cháng Bǎi: contemplating own-marks gives understanding but does not cut affliction; that requires the shared marks.

"Delusion cannot delude delusion": Master Cháng Bǎi parses it: ignorance cannot produce itself; it arises from conditions. Consciousness has no real "flowing along" with merit or demerit; Venerable Miào Jìng: "if it really had that nature, it would be conjoined at all times."

Without a self, how does self-view arise? Through its object (the ālayavijñāna), its support, its cause, and its result. Self-view is "known only through one's own inner experience"; Venerable Miào Jìng: chiefly the manas, the seventh consciousness, whose grasping we do not even notice.

"This pool sends forth many streams": Venerable Miào Jìng: the pool is the ālayavijñāna; the streams are the three realms and five destinies. Liberation is release from afflictions, "neither before nor after". Master Cháng Bǎi: manas and its afflictions arise and cease together; when they cease, the mind is simply free.

The verses end: "simply the exhaustion of all suffering". Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only the many sufferings are exhausted; the uncontaminated virtues are not; they remain." Liberation is not annihilation.

quiz.q: "Resting on two classes … heedless towards objects, advancing on a wrong path." Where does Venerable Miào Jìng say a householder's defilement comes from?
options: householders live in craving; all their defilement comes from craving
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Householders live in craving, so all their defilements come from craving." The renunciant class's defilement is ignorance — wrong advancement. The treatise assigns each separately.

quiz.q: "Because of two root afflictions, the twelve links divide into two." What does each govern, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: in the twelve links, ignorance is strongest in initiating karma, craving in moistening it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "In the twelve links, ignorance is most powerful in initiating karma, craving most powerful in moistening it." The caused dharmas are the first seven links; the caused sufferings the last five.

quiz.q: The five similes contemplate own-marks; "arise and cease together" contemplates the shared mark. How does Master Cháng Bǎi divide their roles?
options: contemplating own-marks only gives understanding and doesn't cut affliction; cutting affliction needs the shared mark
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Contemplating this way only gives understanding; it can't yet cut affliction — that requires contemplating the shared mark." Venerable Miào Jìng: arising, abiding, ceasing is the contemplation of impermanence.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi parse "delusion cannot delude delusion"?
options: the first 癡 is a verb, the second a noun; ignorance can't produce itself — it arises from conditions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The first 癡 is a verb, the second a noun. Ignorance cannot arise by itself; it is born of conditions." The lectures read 非餘能有癡 as "it doesn't belong to others free of delusion," unlike the English.

quiz.q: Self-view is "known only through one's own inner experience." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say this mainly refers to?
options: chiefly the manas, the seventh consciousness — whose discerning we ourselves don't even notice
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'Known through one's own inner experience' mainly refers to manas, the seventh consciousness; we ourselves can't perceive its discerning." Master Cháng Bǎi: innate self-view is the seventh grasping the eighth.

quiz.q: "This pool sends forth many streams." What do the pool and streams stand for, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the pool is the store-consciousness; the many streams are the three realms and five destinies
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The pool is the store-consciousness; 'sends forth many streams' — the water flowing out stands for the three realms and five destinies." Only the true Dharma can dry it.

quiz.q: "Simply the exhaustion of all suffering" can sound like annihilation. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: only suffering ends; uncontaminated virtues do not and remain — the text uses this to refute "mere nonexistence"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only the many sufferings are exhausted; the uncontaminated virtues are not — they remain. That's the flavour of this phrase." Master Cháng Bǎi: the remainderless is not utter nothingness.
